title: Recognize a kernel-killing generator telescope comparison
statement: Let $C$ be triangulated [def-weil-triangulated-category], with morphism universe $v$ and coproducts indexed by types in universe $\max(w,v)$. Let $E_i$, $i\in I$ with $I$ in that universe, be compact [def-pc-compact-object], and suppose their coproduct is a weak generator [def-pc-generators]. Let $Y,H\in C$, $X_n\in C$, $t_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$, and $f_n:X_n\to Y$. Suppose every $g:E_i[m]\to Y$ factors through $f_0$, and every $g:E_i[m]\to X_n$ with $f_n\circ g=0$ satisfies $t_n\circ g=0$. Write $A=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf N}X_n$, with coprojections $j_n$, and let $s:A\to A$ have $s\circ j_n=j_{n+1}\circ t_n$. Suppose $A\xrightarrow{1-s}A\xrightarrow{q}H\xrightarrow{r}A[1]$ is distinguished and $c:H\to Y$ satisfies $c\circ q\circ j_n=f_n$ for all $n$. Then $c$ is an isomorphism. No coproduct presentation of the stages or transition cones is assumed.

proof.text: Set ι_n equal to the nth coprojection followed by q. Restrict the zero composite in the telescope triangle to each coprojection and expand identity minus shift. This gives t_n followed by ι_(n+1) equal to ι_n.

proof.text: Prove compactness of E_i[m] from the definition: use the additive shift adjunction, DirectSum.congrAddEquiv on its Hom equivalences, and postcomposition with the inverse coproduct comparison of the inverse shift. Check commutativity on each direct-sum summand using adjunction naturality. The shifted compactness map is conjugate to the original bijection. This is the proved compact_shift argument of BrownTelescopeAssembly, generalized to coproduct universe max w v; no Brown theorem is assumed.

proof.text: Convert (X_n,t_n) into Functor.ofSequence t. Apply the compact-Hom homotopy-colimit comparison to E_i[m]. Its surjectivity and Types.jointly_surjective' give factorization of every map E_i[m] to H through a stage.

proof.text: Postcomposition with c is bijective on Hom(E_i[m],H). Initial lifting and the comparison equations give surjectivity. If a has zero composite with c, write a as b followed by ι_n. The comparison equation gives b followed by f_n zero. Kernel killing and transition compatibility give a zero. Apply this zero-kernel assertion to the difference of two maps to obtain injectivity.

source.place: Tag 09SN, Lemma lemma-write-as-colimit, proof: comparison map and vanishing of its cone

proof.text: For any target shift n, the adjunction between shifts -n and n and the source shift-addition isomorphism identify postcomposition with c[n] with the preceding bijective map for E_i[m-n]. Naturality of the adjunction proves this identification; hence all these shifted Hom maps are bijective.

source.place: Tag 09SN, Lemma lemma-write-as-colimit, proof: comparison map and vanishing of its cone

proof.text: Complete c to a distinguished triangle H → Y → D → H[1]. A map E_i[m] → D has zero composite to H[1], since its composite with c[1] is zero and postcomposition with c[1] is injective. Hom exactness factors it through Y. Surjectivity for c lifts that factor through H; the consecutive composite H → Y → D is zero, so the original map vanishes. Shift adjunction makes every map E_i → D[n] zero. If D were nonzero, generation would give a nonzero map from the coproduct of E_i to some D[n], contradicting coproduct extensionality. Thus D is zero. Mathlib Triangle.isZero₃_iff_isIso₁ applied to this triangle gives IsIso c.

theorem compactGenerator_telescope_isIso
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ]
    [Preadditive C] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive]
    [Pretriangulated C] [IsTriangulated C] [HasCoproducts.{max w v} C]
    {I : Type (max w v)} (E : I → C)
    (hcompact : ∀ i : I, IsCompactObject (E i))
    (hgenerate : IsTriangulatedGeneratingFamily E)
    (Y : C) (X : ℕ → C) (t : ∀ n : ℕ, X n ⟶ X (n + 1))
    (f : ∀ n : ℕ, X n ⟶ Y)
    (hstart : ∀ (i : I) (m : ℤ) (g : (E i)⟦m⟧ ⟶ Y),
      ∃ a : (E i)⟦m⟧ ⟶ X 0, a ≫ f 0 = g)
    (hkill : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : I) (m : ℤ) (g : (E i)⟦m⟧ ⟶ X n),
      g ≫ f n = 0 → g ≫ t n = 0)
    (H : C)
    (q : (∐ fun n : ULift.{max w v} ℕ => X n.down) ⟶ H)
    (r : H ⟶ (∐ fun n : ULift.{max w v} ℕ => X n.down)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hT : Triangle.mk
      (𝟙 (∐ fun n : ULift.{max w v} ℕ => X n.down) -
        Sigma.desc (fun n : ULift.{max w v} ℕ =>
          t n.down ≫ Sigma.ι (fun k : ULift.{max w v} ℕ => X k.down)
            ⟨n.down + 1⟩)) q r ∈ distTriang C)
    (c : H ⟶ Y)
    (hstage : ∀ n : ℕ,
      Sigma.ι (fun k : ULift.{max w v} ℕ => X k.down) ⟨n⟩ ≫ q ≫ c = f n) :
    IsIso c
